uncited: This method is a specific implementation detail of the rasterization step in [Gaussian Splatting](946-gaussian-splatting.md), distinct from alternative rasterization strategies like [Ray-marching on 3D Gaussians](1036-ray-marching-on-3d-gaussians.md) or [2D Gaussian Projection with Covariance Stabilization](1198-2d-gaussian-projection-with-covariance-stabilization.md).

- **Input**: A projected Gaussian primitive $p$ with screen-space center $(sx, sy)$, bounding box $[x_0, y_0, x_1, y_1]$, inverse covariance matrix elements $a, b, d$ (where $a = \Sigma^{-1}_{0,0}$, $b = \Sigma^{-1}_{0,1} = \Sigma^{-1}_{1,0}$, $d = \Sigma^{-1}_{1,1}$), opacity $\alpha_p$, and color $C_p$.
- $a, b, d$ are elements of the inverse covariance matrix
- **Time Complexity**: Reduces the number of multiplications and additions per pixel in the inner loop by hoisting row-constant terms.
The exact reduction depends on the number of operations moved outside the loop.
- **Memory Complexity**: No additional memory required beyond precomputed row constants, which are stored in registers or local variables.
- **Measured Performance**: Not given in the sources.
More efficient for large splats covering many pixels.
Requires careful handling of bounding boxes and edge cases.
- **When to Use**: When rasterizing many large Gaussians and performance is critical.
- **When Not to Use**: For very small splats or when other parts of the pipeline are the bottleneck.
Row-constant hoisting is an optimization technique applied to Gaussian splatting rasterization.
The technique leverages the mathematical structure of the 2D Gaussian function to minimize redundant calculations.
